record.paper_title: Two open problems in precedence constrained scheduling
record.context_brief: single-machine total tardiness with chain-like precedence
record.original_question: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. There are n jobs, all available at time 0, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Every job has unit processing time, and each job j has an integer due date d_j. The precedence constraints are chain-like: in the directed precedence graph on the jobs, each vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one. A feasible schedule is a permutation σ of the jobs that respects the precedence constraints, meaning σ(j) < σ(k) whenever (j,k) is a precedence arc. If job j is scheduled in position σ(j), then its tardiness is max(0, σ(j) - d_j). What is the complexity of finding a precedence-feasible schedule minimizing the total tardiness over all jobs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following scheduling problem. There are $n$ jobs, all available at time $0$, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Every job has unit processing time, and each job $j \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ has an associated integer due date $d_j$. Precedence constraints are given by a directed graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ in which every vertex has indegree at most $1$ and outdegree at most $1$ (so $G$ is a disjoint union of directed chains). A feasible schedule is a permutation $\sigma : \{1,\dots,n\} \to \{1,\dots,n\}$ such that $\sigma(j) < \sigma(k)$ whenever $(j,k)$ is an arc of $G$; here $\sigma(j)$ denotes the position (equivalently, the completion time) of job $j$. The tardiness of job $j$ in schedule $\sigma$ is $\max\{0,\sigma(j) - d_j\}$, and the total tardiness is $\sum_{j=1}^{n} \max\{0, \sigma(j) - d_j\}$.

Determine the computational complexity of finding a feasible permutation $\sigma$ that minimizes the total tardiness. In particular, decide whether this problem is solvable in polynomial time or is NP-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on the scheduling literature (in standard notation, the problem 1 | chains, p_j = 1 | ∑T_j) do not turn up a known complexity classification. Surveys list NP-hardness for closely related variants such as the weighted-tardiness version, the number-of-late-jobs criterion with chains, and position-based weighted objectives, but the unweighted total-tardiness case with unit jobs and chain precedence is not stated as resolved. Its status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An Overview of Some Single Machine Scheduling Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses 1||∑T_j as NP-hard and various unit-time tardiness variants, but does not state a complexity result for 1|chains,p_j=1|∑T_j.
status_evidence.claim: The complexity of total tardiness with unit jobs and chain precedence is not given a known classification in this recent overview.

status_evidence.title: Complexity results for scheduling chains on a single machine
status_evidence.snippet: NP-hardness is established for the cases in which the number of late jobs or the total weighted tardiness is to be minimized.
status_evidence.claim: Related variants (number of late jobs; total weighted tardiness) under chains with unit jobs are NP-hard, but the unweighted total tardiness case is not settled there.

status_evidence.title: Polyhedral results for position-based scheduling of chains on a single machine
status_evidence.snippet: 1|chains,p_j=1|∑w_{j,σ_j} is NP-hard in the strong sense, even if each chain has only two jobs.
status_evidence.claim: A more general position-based weighted version is NP-hard, leaving the unweighted total tardiness variant as a separate, apparently unresolved question.
